title: Deep phenotyping of the unselected COPSAC2010 birth cohort study.
ehr_evidence: All information was obtained by personal interview at clinical visits by medical doctors (MDs) and research assistants both with paediatric training. Medical, familial, environmental, and socio-economic histories were assessed by predeﬁned questions and closed response categories and entered online into a dedicated database running an audit trail (Oracle database on a Novel SQL server).
summary: Cohort description of the COPSAC 2010 birth study, detailing recruitment, deep phenotyping protocols, biobanking, and embedded randomized controlled trials investigating perinatal exposures and genetic interactions on childhood allergic and inflammatory diseases.
key_findings: 738 mothers were recruited from week 24 of gestation, and 700 of their children were included in the birth cohort.
Adherence was high with 685 children (98%) attending the 1 year clinic visit and 667 children (95%) attending the 2 year visit.
Participants had a higher prevalence of asthma, eczema, and hayfever, and higher income/education levels compared to non-participants.
study_design: prospective longitudinal birth cohort study with embedded randomized controlled trials
population: unselected cohort of pregnant women and their offspring in eastern Denmark, followed from pregnancy/infancy to age 3+ years
exposure_domain: perinatal exposures, human microbiome, maternal nutrition, environmental factors, medications
limitations: recruitment bias towards higher socioeconomic status
primary outcome data not yet analyzed
